outcomes.description: Distinguish source wording, assumptions, reasoning and gaps in the evidence.

manifest.course_name: Demo / Literature: Two readings of The Window

records.title: The Window: Waiting for contact
records.text: The open window, empty chair and unsent letter suggest a speaker waiting for contact. The key outside complicates that reading.
limitations: This is one interpretation of the teaching poem. The exercise has no official answer or definitive statement of authorial intent.

records.title: The Window: Lines from the English translation
records.text:
The Window. English translation of an original Chinese teaching poem generated by the ExamSage project on 16 November 2026.
1 The rain has stopped. The window is still open.
2 In the lamplight the empty chair becomes an unsent letter.
3 I put the key back outside the door.
4 The wind gave no answer.

records.title: The Window: A reading of departure
records.text: The key outside and the unanswering wind can suggest departure. The open window offers evidence against complete isolation.

records.title: Discussion question
records.text: Using only this poem, distinguish a quoted line, an interpretation and counterevidence.

records.title: Part a
records.text: Compare two readings and give the line numbers supporting each. Explain how the evidence leaves room for more than one interpretation.
